turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Morning. Observations are done. Blood pressure one thirty-six over eighty-four, pulse seventy-two. Medication screen says atorvastatin forty milligrams, for his cholesterol, every day.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's forty, Alan, they increased it last year. I'm Jean, his wife. You'll only get one word out of him.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the dose blank for now. Here for the stomach and the sleep?
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's awake at three a lot of nights. Pain's been six weeks, under the right ribs, sharp. And he's short of breath when it hits.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Middle. Dull. Two weeks. Not breathless.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Two weeks or six, then. Dull, middle of the tummy. Any heartburn?
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Socially, listen to him. Tell the doctor properly, Alan.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): A bottle. Most nights. Perhaps.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thank you. That's worth knowing and I'm not about to lecture you. Do you smoke?
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ever had a camera, an endoscopy?
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. Twenty milligrams, for his stomach.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): There was amitriptyline suggested for sleep. Did you take any?
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, um, the parking meter is running out, and that telly was a dreadful property programme. I'll shut up.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nearly there. Lie back. Tummy's soft, tender in the middle, no guarding. Still no burning after the wine?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Burns. Up in the chest. After the wine.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mornings, are you queasy or not?
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Likely acid, stirred up by the wine. That's provisional. I'll start lansoprazole by mouth, thirty milligrams, once a day, before breakfast.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Liver bloods today, with that drinking. Come back in two weeks.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): And ease off the wine if you can. It might help the sleep as well.
[SEG0052] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll take the liver bloods next door. The form just needs a signature.

spec.situation: Person attending for stomach pain and poor sleep; alcohol answered casually ('socially'), later 'a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps'; doctor non-judgemental; liver blood tests ordered; stomach medicine started.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Omeprazole 20 mg for stomach and stopped in March are supported; dose/indication reported by family, not patient.

omissions.text: Atorvastatin dose on the medication screen was stated as 40 mg daily for cholesterol; the recorded medication entry omits the dose.
Heartburn was specifically asked about and initially denied by the patient before later describing burning up in the chest after wine.
Nausea/feeling sick was specifically asked about and initially denied, then later the patient reported being queasy in the mornings.
The patient denied smoking currently, but was not asked whether he had ever smoked; recording this as smoking status 'never' overstates what was said.
The patient denied prior amitriptyline use for sleep ('Never'), but this negative medication history is not recorded.
